description: Pick a question you genuinely wonder about and carry it for a week, collecting answers slowly. Depth beats speed.

body.heading: Choose a question with roots
paragraphs: The best questions for this are not quick facts but live ones: Why do we say 'bless you' after a sneeze? How does my town get its water? What did this street look like a hundred years ago?
Write the question somewhere you will see it daily: a notebook's first page, a note on the fridge. You are not researching under deadline; you are keeping a question company.

body.heading: Collect, do not just search
paragraphs: Yes, look things up, but also ask people, observe, and notice related things during the week. An answer assembled from a book, a conversation and your own looking is remembered far better than a single search result.
At the week's end, write half a page: what you found, what surprised you, and what the question has grown into. Often the new question it leads to is even better.

takeaway: Carry one good question for a week, and write down where it takes you.
